newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up on institutional support.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up on institutional support.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed higher on Thursday due to institutional demand for stocks with a promising earnings outlook, brokers said.
The B share index firmed 0.67 points, or 0.75 percent, to 89.51, with turnover rising to HK$29.62 million from HK$18.70 million on Wednesday.

Institutional buying emerged in the afternoon session, which boosted market sentiment, one broker said. Another broker said institutional purchasing mainly targeted a handful of issues expected to post solid profits this year.
The index' rise was due to sharp gains by Great Ocean and Victor Onward on speculative buying, brokers said.
Great Ocean surged HK$0.17, or 8.67 percent, to HK$2.13 and Victor Onward rose HK$0.13, or 7.88 percent, to HK$1.78.
Guangdong Power traded the most on volume of 3.74 million shares and rose HK$0.13 to HK$5.42 on demand from institutions, brokers said.
Dadonghai, which had seen steady declines for a few sessions, rebounded HK$0.02 to HK$1.29 in trading of 609,900 shares. It was the second most active counter on Thursday.
Changchai edged up HK$0.02 to HK$5.00 with 450,500 shares traded. The rise was based on investor confidence in the diesel engine maker's results this year, brokers said.
But China Merchants dropped HK$0.07 to HK$3.50 on volume of 228,800 shares.

The A share index continued its upward trend, rising 1.03 points, or 0.28 percent, to 373.07 on turnover of 10.32 billion yuan, compared with 9.31 billion yuan. The composite index added 1.03 points, or 0.30 percent, to close at 347.57.
Buying was focused on Shenzhen-based counters, with Shenzhen Zhonghao soaring 0.85 yuan, or 12.01 percent, to 7.93 yuan.
